content: I have been developing a formalization of Boolean-valued models of ZF(C) for about a month. The long-term goal is Boolean-valued analysis and a formalization of Gordon's theorem. My project is pinned to 4.32.1, but CI is configured to audit the project against whatever Tau Ceti is using at the time of the run. This was done in order to facilitate potential Tau Ceti integration at some stage. However, I do not know if such a thing would be useful to the project. As far as I can tell, Tau Ceti seems mainly concerned with algebraic geometry and related disciplines. Therefore I have made no noise on the Tau Ceti repo.

Steve Sabean said:

Tau Ceti seems mainly concerned with algebraic geometry and related disciplines. Therefore I have made no noise on the Tau Ceti repo.

I think this is just a consequence of who's been making roadmaps. I think more roadmaps in other areas are definitely welcome.

Hi Chris. Thanks for the info. I just finished formalizing a proof of Δ0\Delta_0Δ0​ (set-bounded) absoluteness. The next dragon to slay is proving a fragment of ZF and providing a soundness argument. My tentative plan was to draft a roadmap according to TC specifications after that, so that a reference implementation actually does something real and recognizable.

@Steve Sabean, yes, it would be great to have a roadmap here, but I do want to make sure that it focuses on the basics and covers the basics thoroughly, before we get on to anything exciting. :-)

After consulting my AI, how about a roadmap that covers:

  1. Complete Boolean algebras: antichains, maximal antichains, partitions of unity and refinement.
  2. B-valued names: the rank recursion, the mutually recursive truth values of equality and membership, canonical names, and the quotient by equality of value 1.
  3. Truth values for arbitrary formulas, and soundness.
  4. The mixing and maximum principles.
  5. Verification that each axiom of ZFC has truth value 1.
  6. Bounded absoluteness, and ascent and descent: of sets, maps, relations and algebraic structures, with the identities relating the two.
  7. The internal number systems ℕ, ℤ, ℚ, ℝ, the least upper bound property, and the dense embedding of the ground model reals.
  8. Vector lattices: disjointness, bands, the projection theorem for Dedekind complete lattices, band projections as a complete Boolean algebra, weak order units and components, lateral and universal completeness.
  9. Gordon's theorem: the descended reals form a universally complete vector lattice, and b ↦ χ(b) is an isomorphism of B onto its band projections.

Just remember the goals for Tau Ceti roadmaps should primarily be thorough and high quality coverage rather than aiming at particular endpoints or theorems. Rising sea and all that.

Hi @Kim Morrison
Thanks for your response.
That sounds excellent, and the emphasis on covering the basics thoroughly is helpful. I can draft the roadmap along those lines.

By happy coincidence, quite a bit of 2–6 is already present in the current implementation: Boolean-valued names with equality/membership and canonical names; the quotient by equality of value 1; truth values for arbitrary first-order formulas; mixing and the maximum principle; Δ₀/bounded absoluteness; and the beginnings of ascent/descent. I also just finished Boolean validity of Extensionality, Empty Set, Pairing, and Union, so item 5 is underway. Soundness and the remaining ZFC axioms are still substantial gaps.

Item 1 is a useful correction to my present organization. I have partitions of unity and maximal-antichain/Zorn machinery because they were needed for mixing and the maximum principle, but I have not treated antichains, refinement, etc. as a polished standalone piece of complete Boolean-algebra theory. I agree that they should come first rather than appear merely as implementation details.

I’ll therefore treat the existing code as a source of tested constructions rather than as determining the roadmap order, and aim for a roadmap whose milestones build the general theory in roughly the sequence you suggest. The internal number systems/vector-lattice/Gordon part also matches the eventual direction I had in mind, but I’m very happy to keep that firmly downstream of a thorough foundations layer.
